params.message:
Pace each Claude account's week evenly, and drop the peak-hour brake

The plan the two Claude logins are on no longer has a five-hour session
limit; the weekly limit stays. The session cap braked bursts by itself.
Without it one re-tag or bench run can spend an account's week in a day
or two, and with both accounts refused every Claude phase stops until
the reset, so the later days of the week are classified and enriched
late or not at all.

spend.mjs: the daily ceiling (SPEND_DAILY_USD) becomes a weekly budget
per account (SPEND_WEEKLY_USD, default 350 notional dollars), paced
evenly. The background may have spent (budget - reserve) x the elapsed
share of the week plus a burst allowance of at most a day's share. The
week runs from the account's own reset when known (read from the CLI's
refusal, kept in account_weeks), otherwise it is the rolling last seven
days. A reserve (default a tenth) is left for the interactive paths.

Lanes: background (engine, crons) is paced; every server request runs
in the interactive lane and is not paced; bulk jobs (retag-cohort,
bench, eval-models, or SPEND_LANE=bulk) wait while an account is on or
above its even line. accountsToTry skips an account at pace, so calls
move to the other one; with all at pace callCli throws a paced error
and the scoring drops paid actions, classify included.

The supervisor's peak-hour brake (weekdays 13:00-19:00 GMT, two workers,
expensiveDiscount x 0.7) existed only for the session limit and is gone.
Its rule now lives in supervisor-decide.mjs so it is tested as it runs.

Shown in /llm-health, /accounts, the supervisor state, /api/elixir
(extra.spend*, spendAccounts) and on the wall: a finding when an account
runs ahead of pace for six hours, or is refused on its weekly limit.
